Haradah
hah-RAY-dah
proper noun
Hebrew charadah, “fear” or “trembling,” from a root meaning to tremble or be afraid, a station of Israel in the wilderness wandering.

📖 Biblical Definition

Haradah is one of the encampments of the children of Israel in the wilderness, recorded by Moses in the itinerary of their journeys which he wrote at the commandment of the LORD (Num 33:24-25). They came to it from mount Shapher, and from Haradah they removed and pitched in Makheloth. The name signifies “fear” or “trembling,” from a root that speaks of a great quaking or terror, and though the Scripture records no event that gave the place its name, the word itself is a sober one for a halting-place in the long wandering. The dictionary will not invent a history where the LORD has left silence; it honours that even a camp called Trembling was a station appointed by Him who led His people through the great and terrible wilderness. Fear there was in plenty in that desert, of serpents and of scorpions and of drought, and of the wrath of God against a murmuring generation; yet through it all the LORD forsook them not, but His pillar of cloud and of fire departed not from them. Haradah stands as a witness that the people of God pass through places of fear in their pilgrimage, yet are not consumed, for the LORD their God is in the midst of them. The pilgrim whose heart trembles in the dark valley may remember that the Shepherd who led Israel through Haradah leads His sheep through the valley of the shadow, and they need fear no evil, for He is with them.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A station of Israel in the wilderness, between mount Shapher and Makheloth, its name signifying fear.

expand to see more

HARADAH, a station of the children of Israel in the wilderness, signifying “fear” or “trembling.”

They removed from mount Shapher and encamped in Haradah.

From Haradah they journeyed and pitched in Makheloth.

Its name springs from a root meaning to tremble or be afraid.

It witnesses to the LORD’s keeping of His people through places of fear.

📖 Key Scripture

Num 33:24 — "And they removed from mount Shapher, and encamped in Haradah."

Num 33:25 — "And they removed from Haradah, and pitched in Makheloth."

Deu 8:15 — "Who led thee through that great and terrible wilderness, wherein were fiery serpents, and scorpions, and drought, where there was no water; who brought thee forth water out of the rock of flint;"

Psa 23:4 — "Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A place of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses to the LORD’s keeping of His people through places of fear.

expand to see more

Haradah is a name of the wilderness itinerary, and no movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine it. The dictionary records it that the reader who meets the name among the stations of Israel may know it for a real place in a real journey, where a real God led His trembling people through the great and terrible wilderness.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the presence of God with His people in their fear. He who led Israel through the camp called Trembling, through fiery serpents and drought, is the same who walks with His own through the valley of the shadow of death. The pilgrim whose heart quakes in the dark may remember Haradah, a name of fear in the wilderness, yet a station where the pillar of cloud departed not, and may say with David, I will fear no evil, for thou art with me.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “fear,” Haradah names a station of Israel between mount Shapher and Makheloth.

expand to see more

Haradah — Hebrew charadah, “fear” or “trembling.”

It was a station of Israel in the wilderness wandering.

They removed from mount Shapher and encamped in Haradah.

From thence they journeyed to Makheloth.

Its root speaks of a great quaking or terror.

Usage

"Like Israel at Haradah, the people of God pass through places of fear, yet are not consumed, for He is with them."

"The LORD who led His people through the great and terrible wilderness forsakes them not in the valley of the shadow."

"A camp called Trembling is yet a station appointed by the God who keeps His own through every fear."
